gloss: to win; to gain; to earn (popularity, fame)

definitions.gloss: to win, to gain, to earn
definitions.explanation: To acquire or earn something positive such as popularity, fame, sympathy, or acclaim. Almost always used with abstract nouns denoting favorable reception.

examples.japanese: その{映画|えいが}は{世界中|せかいじゅう}で{好評|こうひょう}を{博|はく}した。
examples.english: The film earned acclaim throughout the world.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{演説|えんぜつ}は{聴衆|ちょうしゅう}の{共感|きょうかん}を{博|はく}し、{大|おお}きな{拍手|はくしゅ}が{起|お}きた。
examples.english: His speech won the audience's sympathy and drew a great round of applause.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{人気|にんき}を{博|はく}する (gain popularity)
・{好評|こうひょう}を{博|はく}する (earn favorable reception)
・{共感|きょうかん}を{博|はく}する (win sympathy)
・{名声|めいせい}を{博|はく}する (earn fame)
・{喝采|かっさい}を{博|はく}する (win applause)

USAGE NOTES:
A formal, written-style verb that always takes を. The object is almost always an abstract noun related to positive reception or reputation. Rarely used in casual conversation — {得|え}る or もらう would be more natural in everyday speech. The past form {博|はく}した is especially common in news and reviews.
